strings.name: Rahul Gandhi
strings.role: Leader of the Opposition in India’s Lok Sabha; former Congress president
strings.summary: Rahul Gandhi is an Indian National Congress politician who has repeatedly been elected to the Lok Sabha since 2004 and became its Leader of the Opposition in 2024. A former Congress vice-president and president, he promotes employment, social equity and government accountability through parliamentary work, campaigning and journeys across regions. His career includes political mobilisation, electoral defeats, changes in party leadership and an interruption of parliamentary membership following a defamation conviction. Opposition leadership is distinct from heading the government or currently serving as party president.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026, including reports of his Hyderabad speech on 14 November and Columbia University appearance on 17 November. Gazette notifications distinguish effective dates from announcement dates. A stay of conviction, restoration of parliamentary membership and a final acquittal are treated separately; political assessments remain attributed to the party or speaker.
strings.influence.rationale: Through long involvement in Congress and opposition politics, electoral campaigning and public mobilisation, he influences debates on Indian democracy and social policy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and current constituency
strings.facts.f1.value: Born on 19 June 1970 to Rajiv Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi. He represents Rae Bareli in Uttar Pradesh and is in his fifth Lok Sabha term. His resignation from the Wayanad seat took effect on 18 June 2024 and was announced in the House on 24 June; older biographies naming Wayanad are not current constituency records.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early career
strings.facts.f2.value: He completed his undergraduate degree at Rollins College in the United States in 1994 and received an MPhil in Development Studies at Trinity College, Cambridge, in 1995. He attended Harvard but did not graduate there. Before entering politics, he worked for the management consultancy Monitor Group in London. An MPhil is not a doctorate.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Speech at the Hyderabad summit
strings.highlights.h1.text: He addressed the closing session of the Bharat Summit on 14 November 2026, discussing opposition strategy, non-violence and relations between politics and business. He also joined activities involving platform workers that day. Allegations of electoral manipulation and business–political ties remain his political claims, not independently established findings merely because they were reported.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Discusses employment and education in New York
strings.highlights.h2.text: At a Columbia University event on 17 November 2026, he discussed employment and education challenges facing Indian youth. Reporting the next day also recorded the BJP’s response. His description of economic risk is an assessment; a separately announced Chicago appearance is not thereby established as having occurred.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Recognised as Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
strings.timeline.t1.text: A Gazette notification dated 26 June confirmed the Speaker’s recognition under the relevant 1977 law, with effect from 9 June. This parliamentary leadership position is distinct from Congress president and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Lok Sabha membership restored
strings.timeline.t2.text: Following the Supreme Court’s stay of his defamation conviction on 4 August, the Lok Sabha Secretariat announced that his earlier disqualification ceased to operate, subject to further judicial decisions. The trial conviction on 23 March, disqualification notification on 24 March, August court relief and parliamentary reinstatement are separate events; they do not amount to a final acquittal.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Launches the Bharat Jodo Yatra
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Bharat Jodo Yatra began at Kanyakumari in southern India and concluded in Kashmir on 30 January 2023, with social unity and public engagement as political aims. The journey and its subsequent political effects require separate assessment; organisers’ accounts of success are not independent impact audits.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Publicly confirms resignation as Congress president
strings.timeline.t4.text: He released his resignation letter, accepting political responsibility for the general-election defeat. He had offered to resign on 25 May, but party colleagues had resisted. That year he lost Amethi and won Wayanad; leaving the party presidency did not mean leaving the Lok Sabha.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Takes over as Congress president
strings.timeline.t5.text: He succeeded Sonia Gandhi in leading the Indian National Congress, with his presidency continuing into 2019. This was a party leadership role, not the presidency of India, the premiership or the parliamentary speakership.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Congress vice-president
strings.timeline.t6.text: After responsibilities for youth and student organisations, he entered a more senior party leadership position. His appointment as vice-president was a separate stage from becoming president in 2017.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Appointed AICC general secretary
strings.timeline.t7.text: He became general secretary of the All India Congress Committee, responsible for the Indian Youth Congress and National Students’ Union of India. Organisational expansion and youth representation were areas of party work; membership-growth figures in promotional accounts are not treated as independently verified results.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First elected to the Lok Sabha
strings.timeline.t8.text: He entered national parliamentary politics by winning Amethi in Uttar Pradesh. He later represented Wayanad and retained Rae Bareli from 2024. The Lok Sabha is India’s lower house, distinct from the Rajya Sabha and state legislatures.
